system_description.narrative_title: Fragmented great-power competition amid economic warfare and market stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is in flux as simultaneous kinetic conflicts (notably in Iran and Ukraine), expanding sanctions and economic warfare, and renewed US–China strategic rivalry interact to reshape geopolitics. Financial markets and central-bank policy shifts (Warsh/Jackson Hole) amplify economic spillovers through energy, food and capital flows, forcing states and corporations to reconfigure supply chains, finance, and alliances. Military postures and coalition politics are adjusting across theaters (NATO, Baltic, Indo‑Pacific), while secondary states and financial hubs are drawn into sanction, trade and investment contests.
system_description.scope: Interstate conflict and military posture (Iran war, Russia–Ukraine, regional strikes); great-power competition (US–China strategic, trade and tech rivalry); global financial and debt markets, central-bank policy and bond-market stress; sanctions, trade measures and financial infrastructure; energy, food and commodity supply chains; multinational corporations and strategic industries (tech, defense, finance).
system_description.super_system: The integrated global political‑economic system — the international order linking states, markets, and planetary resource and ecological constraints.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial system and capital markets

variables.name: Iran regional war and blockade
variables.description: Iran’s confrontation with the United States and regional actors is evolving into a costly, protracted stalemate marked by maritime interdiction, attacks on energy flows and concerted measures to squeeze Tehran’s economy.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war and European security
variables.description: Russia’s large‑scale campaign against Ukraine and the sustained Western military, financial and diplomatic support for Kyiv are driving escalatory military intensity, humanitarian destruction and an uneven mix of battlefield pressure and intermittent diplomacy.

variables.name: U.S.–China strategic and economic rivalry
variables.description: The United States and China are locked in a widening strategic competition spanning trade, high‑tech supply chains, export controls and military posturing around Taiwan and maritime Asia, reshaping investment, industrial policy and security alignments.

variables.name: Global financial and monetary tensions
variables.description: Volatility in U.S. monetary policy and Treasury markets, rising bond yields and debates over dollar primacy are reconfiguring global capital flows, investor behaviour and central‑bank strategies across advanced and emerging economies.

variables.name: Global energy realignment and access competition
variables.description: Major powers and energy firms are reordering access to oil and gas — from new bilateral deals to shifts in OPEC+ influence and production disruptions — altering market power, investment patterns and geopolitical alignments in the energy arena.
